clue.text: Dynamo in our wee shop malfunctioned

indicators.note: something that has malfunctioned has gone wrong, so the letters before it are out of order

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A generator, or perhaps an energetic shopkeeper, has broken down in a tiny local shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person of tremendous energy and drive, as well as a source of electrical power.

clue.text: Page on amateur stage production

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
lay means non-professional, amateur

explanation.surface: A page boy appears in an amateur dramatic show.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts P above LAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a drama written for performance in a theatre, so a production on stage.

clue.text: Wife saying yes, rolling about in mud

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
allowing means permitting, saying yes

explanation.surface: A wife agrees to a romp in the mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallowing is how pigs and buffalo lie and roll in mud or water to cool off.

clue.text: Admire skill and integrity

parts.note: to respect someone is to admire them
ability means skill

explanation.surface: We look up to people of talent and honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admire skill and integrity' reads as a list of virtues; 'and' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectability is the quality of being decent and upstanding, close to honesty and moral uprightness.

clue.text: Single over American finds difficult

parts.note: a oner is a single unique thing or person, British slang
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: An American watching cricket finds a single over hard to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: A oner is British slang for something unique, one of a kind; an over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Onerous means burdensome and demanding effort, so hard or difficult to bear.

clue.text: Language used within confines of stag party

indicators.note: used within means placed inside, so one piece goes into another
the confines of a word are its boundaries, meaning its first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters of stag
Hindi is a major language of India

explanation.surface: Bad language heard at a bachelor party.
explanation.walkthrough: HINDI goes between S and G. A stag party is the British name for a bachelor party; 'stag party' looks like the definition, but only 'party' is.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal word for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Luxurious hotel cut credit

indicators.note: cut means removed, so the abbreviation for the hotel is taken out of the first word

parts.note: plush means opulent, luxurious
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A posh hotel has made cutbacks and stopped offering credit.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the H out of PLUSH to leave PLUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or point in someone's favour, as is a credit on a record.

clue.text: Large Italian male, supple

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large
It is the abbreviation for Italian
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A big Italian man who is surprisingly agile.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe describes a body that is flexible and graceful, bending easily.

clue.text: Extra portions of food team ruins

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
to dish someone's chances is to ruin them

explanation.surface: A team wrecks the extra helpings at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dishes' as a verb meaning ruins is informal, as in dishing one's hopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Side dishes are smaller accompaniments served alongside a main course.

clue.text: Ordinary study in B & B, say

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here between the two halves of the lodging abbreviation

parts.note: B & B written out with the ampersand as AND
to read a subject is to study it
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A student staying at a bed and breakfast, reading something mundane.
explanation.walkthrough: B & B is bed and breakfast, a small British guesthouse; the ampersand is read out as the word and. 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread-and-butter, as an adjective, describes everyday, basic or routine things.

clue.text: Book finally abridged

indicators.note: an abridged text is shortened, so the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: at last is a two-word phrase meaning finally

explanation.surface: A long book has at last been cut down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: AT LAST shortened by its last letter gives ATLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound volume of maps, so it is one kind of book.

clue.text: Moved abroad, head of group settled in Abu Dhabi with daughter?

indicators.note: to settle in a place is to go inside it, so one letter is placed within the next piece

parts.note: Abu Dhabi is one of the United Arab Emirates; the question mark flags it as an example

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of group
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone emigrated: a group leader settled in the Gulf with their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Abu Dhabi is one of the seven emirates of the UAE, hence the question mark for a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's own country to live in another, so moving abroad.

clue.text: Run out of ideas, so planned tea dance doomed?

indicators.note: something planned has been arranged, so the following letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Organisers short of fresh ideas fear their planned tea dance is a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to a dead end is an idiom for reaching a point where no further progress or ideas are possible.

clue.text: Vacation so relaxing in Canadian province

indicators.note: relaxing loosens things up, so the letters are freed into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A holiday that is so restful, spent in eastern Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Nova Scotia is one of Canada's Maritime provinces, on the Atlantic coast, with Halifax as capital.

clue.text: Is a poet on drugs?

indicators.note: being on something suggests being under its influence and so in a disordered state

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A question about whether some writer of verse is high on narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to poets such as Coleridge and De Quincey, famously users of opium.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are narcotic drugs derived from opium, such as morphine and heroin.

clue.text: Good, boy's looks

parts.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
Lance is a boy's name, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: Praise for a lad's appearance: good, the boy's looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy's' could be any name; the possessive S is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Glances are brief looks, so the plural noun matches the plural noun in the clue.

clue.text: I may not give you a fair deal

definitions.text: I may not give you a fair deal

parts.words: I may not give you a fair deal
parts.note: surface reading: a trader or salesman admitting they might overcharge you
setter's reading: dealing cards, as a cheat at the card table does

explanation.surface: A shady trader warns that their prices may not be honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' suggests a business bargain; it means dealing cards in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a swindler who cheats at cards, often by dealing dishonestly.

clue.text: Lab gear inappropriate for this school subject

indicators.note: something inappropriate is not in its proper place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Laboratory equipment is out of place in a maths lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is a branch of mathematics taught in schools, using letters to stand for numbers.

clue.text: Against carrying on, old merchant of Venice

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so the first piece wraps the next

parts.note: anti means against
taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old trader from Venice opposed to carrying on.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'merchant of Venice' is not the play but its title character.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is the title merchant in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, who borrows from Shylock.

clue.text: Back where witch lived, she with no heart

indicators.note: having no heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: the Witch of Endor is the medium consulted by Saul in the Bible
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tale of a witch's former home, and a heartless woman who once lived there.
explanation.walkthrough: ENDOR is the biblical home of a witch; SHE loses its central H to give SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a proposal or person is to support or approve it, which is to endorse it.

clue.text: One may make one cross, one picking team without leader

indicators.note: without a leader means losing the front, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a selector chooses the members of a sports team

explanation.surface: A team selector annoys a player, making them angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make one cross' suggests angering someone; it means marking a cross on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An elector is a voter, who marks a cross next to the chosen candidate on a ballot.

clue.text: Girl needs chopped apple to make a dessert

indicators.note: something chopped has had its end cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Charlotte is a girl's name
a russet is a variety of apple with rough brownish skin

explanation.surface: A girl must chop up an apple to make a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped apple' sounds like a recipe step; it means RUSSET with its last letter cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte russe is a cold dessert of sponge fingers enclosing a custard or cream filling.

clue.text: A wild urge to contradict

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the letters run out of their order

parts.note: the letters of this word are the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone feels an uncontrollable impulse to disagree.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to dispute or disagree, putting a contrary view against someone.

clue.text: Prince and son depicted by portrait painter

parts.note: Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A prince and his son sit for a painting by a portraitist.
explanation.definitionFit: Frans Hals was a Dutch Golden Age artist celebrated for lively portraits such as The Laughing Cavalier.

clue.text: Well-organised firm — join

parts.note: tight means firm, held fast
to knit is to join or unite closely

explanation.surface: A description of a company that is efficient and wants to merge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a noun for a business; here it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-knit group is closely bonded and well coordinated, so organised effectively.

clue.text: One worn by sailor, a headdress

indicators.note: something worn by a person is carried around by them, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor sporting a fancy headdress.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside TAR to give TIAR, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, a type of headdress.

clue.text: Take off before ten for summit

parts.note: to take off someone is to mimic them, to ape them
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A climber sets off before ten o'clock to reach the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests departing; here it means imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the highest point or tip of something, just as a summit is the top of a mountain.

clue.text: Our Greek primate on board pretended disdain

indicators.note: to be on a vessel is to be inside it, so the other pieces go between the letters of the ship

parts.note: on board conventionally means within SS, the abbreviation for steamship
taken as written
Gr is the abbreviation for Greek
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey from Greece on a ship acted as if it did not care.
explanation.walkthrough: Being on board a ship is a crossword convention for sitting inside SS, so the three pieces are split around by its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour grapes, from Aesop's fox, is an idiom for affecting scorn for something one cannot have.
